newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, led by gold.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Wednesday on good volume, with traders increasingly of the belief the complex may have found a bottom after gold slid back below $350 this week.
"I like the technical aspects in gold and there looks to be strong physical demand in below $350 an ounce," PaineWebber commodities research director, Bernard Savaiko, said.

COMEX April gold found support at $346.30 Tuesday and gained a further $2.50 Wednesday to close at $353.00 an ounce, after seeing a session high at $354.50. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was 60,000 contracts.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $351.80/20, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $346.30 and the New York close Monday around $347.50/50.
"Monday's down day, which took gold back below $350, may have had more to do with Friday's April options expiry, and there was no follow-through since, leaving shorts scrambling for cover," he said.

"There has been producer hedging above $350, with the trade increasing short hedges in the latest CFTC data, and there's been concern about the Swiss more actively managing their gold reserves," he said.
"But the U.S. dollar may have made a top after its multi-year rally, and the bond and stocks market may have already discounted a Fed tightening," he said.
The US February CPI rose 0.3 percent, slightly more than expected, but the core rate, excluding food and energy was unchanged at 0.2 percent, the U.S. Labor Department said Wednesday.
Annual CPI inflation is still running at 3.0 percent, its lowest level in three decades.

Physical gold demand also remains firm, with gold imports to Dubai, a major entrepot distribution center for the Far East, more than doubling to 56.05 tonnes in February, from 23.48 tonnes in the same month last year, according to World Gold Council data released Wednesday.
Also Russia's central bank said Wednesday it aims to boost gold reserves by 90 tonnes in 1997 and 1998.
COMEX May silver ended up 3.7 cents at $5.245 an ounce, after slipping below $5.200 this week for the first time in a month.
NYMEX April platinum closed up $4.40 an ounce at $382.70, while NYMEX June was palladium gained $4.40 also to $149.50.
Workers at Russia's Norilsk metal mine will take part in a national day of protest on March 27, but this would not stop output, union leaders said.
Norilsk workers are also planning a stoppage of April 2 over non-payment of wages.
Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium.
But Russian palladium supplies to Japan are seen resuming in the next few weeks after shipments stopped last December.
Earlier spot palladium prices rose about 35 percent in the first two months of the year to around $160 an ounce, the highest level since June 1995, on the disruption to Russian supplies.
